segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Pippa.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And I'm Georgie. In this programme, we're talking about saving money on food.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Pippa, are you good at saving money on your food shop?

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: I think I'm quite good. I plan what I like to cook so I don't waste money in the supermarket.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: How about you, Georgie?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I'm not very good. I usually go to the supermarket when I'm hungry so I end up buying lots of snacks.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Oh that's a terrible idea. Well in this programme we'll be learning about one way to save money on

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: the food we eat but first I've got a question for you Georgie. The most expensive restaurant

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: in the world is thought to be a restaurant called Sublimotion in Ibiza which only has 12 customers

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: each night. But how much in euros is a meal per person at the restaurant? A, 650 euros,

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: B, 1,650 euros, or C, 2,650

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: euros? The most expensive. I'll go with C, 2,650 euros.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme. Now, food in the UK is getting

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: more expensive as it has been in many parts of the world and some people are struggling to afford

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: their food shopping

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But BBC World Service programme People Fixing the World has been finding out about a project called Bags of Taste which helps people save money on their food shopping and improve their diet at the same time

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Bags of something is an informal way to say a lot of something.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: The founder of Bags of Taste, Alicia Weston, became concerned that people in the UK with less money found it difficult to afford a healthy diet.

segments.speaker: Alicia Weston
segments.text: People in poverty are eating the worst diets and they are getting sicker younger.

segments.speaker: Alicia Weston
segments.text: And we know that diets are the single largest cause of health inequalities in the UK.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Alicia found that people didn't know how to cook the kinds of meals they'd like to eat

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: and they couldn't afford to experiment.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Imagine spending lots of money on ingredients and then wasting them

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: by cooking them badly or burning the food.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: People also thought making healthy food would be too expensive and take too much time.

segments.speaker: Alicia Weston
segments.text: So ultimately, we've been able to come up with a programme that basically can tackle all of these issues.

segments.speaker: Alicia Weston
segments.text: So what we do now is we deliver all the ingredients to their door,

segments.speaker: Alicia Weston
segments.text: because ultimately, behaviour change starts with actually changing your behaviour at home.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Alicia says that ultimately, she's been able to come up with a solution to help people save money on healthy food.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: We can use the adverb ultimately to mean finally, after a series of events have happened.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Alicia wants to tackle the things that stop people eating healthy food on a budget.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: If you tackle a problem, you try to deal with it.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Alicia solution involves delivering ingredients and recipes to people and then using a WhatsApp group to talk to participants Each WhatsApp group has a mentor who shares cooking tips and advice

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: To give you an idea of how this works, the team at People Fixing the World read out some of the messages on one of the Bags of Taste WhatsApp chats.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Amy, mentor.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Remember to put the fridge bag in the fridge.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Can we aim to cook recipe one by Tuesday evening?

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Our first recipe, chana masala, is a classic.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: It needs an onion, which can be a pain to chop, so try our way.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Video posted.

segments.speaker: Ally
segments.text: Ali.

segments.speaker: Ally
segments.text: Love this method.

segments.speaker: Ally
segments.text: Chef emoji.

segments.speaker: Ally
segments.text: First time I've chopped an onion like this and it's so neat and easy.

segments.speaker: Ally
segments.text: Georgia.

segments.speaker: Ally
segments.text: I'm going to cook mine tomorrow, looking forward to it.

segments.speaker: Ally
segments.text: Ali.

segments.speaker: Ally
segments.text: I finished making my chana masala.

segments.speaker: Ally
segments.text: I was a bit too heavy-handed with the chilli.

segments.speaker: Ally
segments.text: My husband likes a lot of spice, so I'd reduce that next time.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: The mentor in the group, Amy, describes the recipe for chana masala as a classic.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We call something a classic to say that it is well known and of good quality.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We can also describe a particular book, film or song as a classic.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Amy sends a video to show a technique for cutting onions, which she describes as a pain to chop.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: If something is a pain to do, it is difficult or annoying to do.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: One of the participants, Ali, said that when she made the chana masala,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: she was a bit heavy with the chilli If you are heavy with an ingredient you use too much of it And so Ali chana masala was very spicy

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Bags of Taste helps people learn new recipes and cook healthy food without spending too much money

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: It's certainly a lot cheaper than a meal at the restaurant in my question, Georgie.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: I asked you how much it costs for a meal at Sublimotion, thought to be the most expensive restaurant in the world.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, I said a meal was €2,650.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Well, you were wrong. It's actually €1,650, but I think that's still pretty expensive.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It definitely is. OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learnt, starting with bags of, which means a lot of something.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: We can use the adverb ultimately to say finally, after a series of events.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: If you tackle a problem, you try to deal with it and find a solution.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: If we describe something like a recipe as a classic, we mean it's well known and of good quality.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: If something is a pain to do, it is annoying or difficult to do.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: And if you are heavy-handed with an ingredient, you use too much of it.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: For example, I made some soup the other day and I was a bit heavy-handed with the salt.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: It tasted disgusting.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Oh, that's not very good.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: OK, once again, our six minutes are up,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: but you can test what you've learned with the interactive quiz on our website.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Visit

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Bye for now.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Bye.
